title: 6 Signs Your Students Like You
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin outlines six reliable signs that students genuinely like a teacher, since students often mask negative feelings but reveal genuine affection more openly. Indicators include students directly telling the teacher they're liked, positive word-of-mouth reaching parents and colleagues, unforced acknowledgement and eagerness for approval, students seeking the teacher out socially during breaks, students calling out greetings across campus even in front of peers, and a felt sense that even a simple warning carries real weight with the class. He frames genuine likability as a major, compoundable advantage in classroom management, distinct from friendship or leniency, and points readers to further resources on building rapport.
points: Notes students are adept at masking negative feelings toward teachers, making genuine positive signals especially valuable to recognize.
Lists direct verbal affirmation and positive word-of-mouth among parents/colleagues as clear indicators of student affection.
Cites unforced acknowledgement and eagerness for approval ('I scored during my soccer game') as signs students feel genuinely connected.
Highlights students seeking out the teacher socially and calling out greetings across campus, even at social risk, as strong signals.
Describes the ultimate sign as a felt sense that even a simple warning carries real weight and meaning with the class.
quotes: Because, you see, students are adept at hiding negative feelings about you.
You’ll hear from all four corners of your classroom, representing your very best students as well as those who struggle.
Which is no small thing. They’ll regard you with some gesture of unforced acknowledgement.
When different groups of students approach you in twos and threes during breaks or before and after school just to talk and laugh, it’s an obvious sign that they like you and enjoy your company.
You can feel, palpably, that even giving a warning matters to your students.
However, whatever level of teaching ability they’ve reached, they can double it in a month by becoming more likable.
